overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of when AI use builds skill and when it erodes it. You'll be asked about cognitive offloading, two controlled studies of learning, the strength of the evidence on skill at work, and habits that preserve skill.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A manager stops remembering meeting times because her calendar app reminds her of each one. What is this an example of?

options.html: Deskilling caused by an AI tutor
options.text: Deskilling caused by an AI tutor
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No tutor is involved, and she never needed to hold meeting times in memory. Using an external aid to reduce the mental work of a task is cognitive offloading.

options.html: Cognitive offloading onto an external aid
options.text: Cognitive offloading onto an external aid
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Cognitive offloading is using a physical action, such as setting a reminder, to reduce the mental work a task requires. The calendar is the external aid.

options.html: A correlation between reminders and memory
options.text: A correlation between reminders and memory
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A correlation is a pattern found across many cases in a study. One person using an external aid to reduce the mental work of a task is cognitive offloading.

options.html: Unaided practice of a skill she needs
options.text: Unaided practice of a skill she needs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Unaided practice means doing a task with no help. She is relying on an external aid to reduce the mental work of a task, which is cognitive offloading.

forms.stemHtml: In a field experiment with nearly a thousand high school mathematics students, some were given a standard chatbot during practice sessions. What happened to those students?

options.html: They scored lower in practice and higher on the later exam
options.text: They scored lower in practice and higher on the later exam
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It was the other way around. With the standard chatbot, practice scores rose 48 percent, and scores on a later exam without AI were 17 percent lower than for students who never had it.

options.html: They scored higher in practice and higher on the later exam
options.text: They scored higher in practice and higher on the later exam
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Only the practice scores rose. On a later exam without AI, these students scored 17 percent lower than students who never had the chatbot.

options.html: They scored the same as students who practiced without AI
options.text: They scored the same as students who practiced without AI
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Their practice scores rose 48 percent, and on a later exam without AI they scored 17 percent lower than students who never had the chatbot.

options.html: They scored higher in practice and lower on the later exam
options.text: They scored higher in practice and lower on the later exam
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Practice scores rose 48 percent with the standard chatbot. On a later exam without AI, those students scored 17 percent lower than students who never had it.

forms.stemHtml: Two controlled studies of students came to opposite headline results about AI and learning. What best explains the difference?

options.html: Whether the tool gave answers or guided practice
options.text: Whether the tool gave answers or guided practice
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The harm came from a chatbot that supplied answers on demand. The benefit came from tutors designed to give hints and keep students doing the work.

options.html: Whether the students were in school or at university
options.text: Whether the students were in school or at university
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The mathematics study found both harm and benefit among the same high school students, depending on the tool. What separated the results was answers on demand versus guided practice.

options.html: Whether the subject was mathematics or physics
options.text: Whether the subject was mathematics or physics
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Within the mathematics study alone, one tool harmed later scores and another didn't. What separated the results was answers on demand versus guided practice.

options.html: Whether the AI model was from 2023 or later
options.text: Whether the AI model was from 2023 or later
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both studies used the same 2023 model. What separated the results was answers on demand versus guided practice.

forms.stemHtml: A survey of 319 knowledge workers found that those with more confidence in AI reported doing less critical thinking. What can this finding show?

options.html: That using AI causes people to think less critically
options.text: That using AI causes people to think less critically
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A survey finding of this kind is a correlation, and it rests on self-report. It shows that the two things go together and can't show that one causes the other.

options.html: That the workers' thinking skills declined over time
options.text: That the workers' thinking skills declined over time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The survey didn't measure skills over time. It shows that confidence in AI and self-reported critical thinking go together, which is a correlation.

options.html: That confidence in AI and reported thinking go together
options.text: That confidence in AI and reported thinking go together
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The finding is a correlation based on what people said about their own thinking. It can't show that AI use causes less critical thinking.

options.html: That AI use is safe for the thinking of all working adults
options.text: That AI use is safe for the thinking of all working adults
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The survey doesn't show safety or harm. It shows that confidence in AI and self-reported critical thinking go together, which is a correlation.

forms.stemHtml: You want to keep your skill at writing clear summaries while still using an AI assistant. Which habits follow from the research on learning with AI? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Writing your own summary before asking the assistant
options.text: Writing your own summary before asking the assistant
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is attempting first: doing your own thinking before you ask for help.

options.html: Asking the assistant to critique your summary
options.text: Asking the assistant to critique your summary
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Asking for a hint or critique keeps you doing the work, as the tutor-style tools in the learning studies did.

options.html: Having the assistant write every summary to save time
options.text: Having the assistant write every summary to save time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Handing over the whole task every time means the skill gets no practice. The habits that follow from the research are attempting first, asking for hints or critique, explaining back, and practicing unaided.

options.html: Writing one summary a week with no AI help at all
options.text: Writing one summary a week with no AI help at all
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is unaided practice: doing the task alone on a schedule to keep the skill in use.

title: Dependence, skill, and learning
